title: Ingest-time catalog gate and canonical performance manifest generator for newly onboarded models
creator: Lina Chen
description: Problem: New model imports vary in metadata completeness and performance measurement, leading to inconsistent catalog entries and unpredictable user experiences when models are pinned. Goal: Implement an ingest-time gate that enforces a canonical performance manifest (manifest-v2) and auto-generates provenance+fingerprint metadata for every newly onboarded model. The gate should run lightweight checks (schema validity, presence of perf baselines for default sequences, quantization flags) and either attach a generated canonical manifest or mark the entry as blocked for manual follow-up. Deliverables: 1) ingest-gate service that validates model manifests and emits a canonical performance manifest (JSON) on success; 2) automated fingerprinting (sha256 of artifact+manifest) used for stable pin IDs; 3) a published docs page + quickstart for model owners describing onboarding expectations; 4) CI lint and a GitHub PR template to attach perf manifests for manual onboarding cases. Acceptance criteria: - All new catalog entries created by the import pipeline include a manifest-v2 file in the model entry in the catalog service. - The ingest-gate rejects imports that lack required perf baselines for the default short/medium/long sequences and returns clear remediation messages. - A deterministic fingerprint is stored in the model record and exposed via the catalog API. - A docs page (docs/model-catalog/ingest-manifests.md) exists and is linked from the onboarding flow. - Integration test coverage for common failure modes and end-to-end smoke test in staging.
comments: 2026-03-01 - Lina Chen: Kickoff. Drafted manifest-v2 schema (fields: model_id, variant_id, architecture, quantization, tokenizer_hash, sequence_profiles: {short,medium,long}, perf_signatures, benchmark_env, run_timestamp, provenance: {source,commit}, fingerprint). Goal is to keep schema small and machine-checkable.

2026-03-03 - Marco Fernández: Research notes: sha256(artifact_binary + manifest_json) gives stable fingerprint even if model hosting URL changes. Need to standardize artifact canonicalization (strip timestamps). Added a short migration plan for existing entries.

2026-03-05 - Eng Lead (Aisha Patel): Approve approach to generate manifests on ingest but require a human-override path for third-party hosted models. Flag: ensure compliance with Private deployment constraints (no external fetch).

2026-03-07 - Marco Fernández: Prototype ingest-gate implemented in model-catalog repo. PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/model-catalog/pull/2423. Prototype returns structured errors that map to UI remediation steps.

2026-03-09 - QA (Jordan Miles): Tests added for missing short/medium/long baselines and for inconsistent tokenizer hashes. Found an edge case where quantized models reported 'q8_0' vs 'q8_0_sparse' — decided to canonicalize quantization tag mapping in the manifest generator.

2026-03-11 - Docs review (Sofia Ramirez): Draft docs in Confluence: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/34567/ingest-manifests. Suggest adding a checklist for community contributors and a sample manifest snippet. Will move to docs repo once schema final.

2026-03-12 - Marco Fernández: Updated ingest-gate to emit a human-readable remediation string and a machine-parsable error code list. Next: integrate with publish pipeline and add end-to-end staging run.
notes: Rollout plan: enable ingest-gate as a soft-warning for 2 weeks (log failures to onboarding channel), then flip to hard-gate after follow-ups and docs are in place.
Migration: backfill manifest-v2 for top 200 most-used models first using existing benchmark artifacts. Record migration run IDs in the model record.
Observability: add a per-import metric with tags: (schema_failure, missing_baseline, fingerprint_mismatch) to track failure modes.
Rollback: ingest-gate is feature-flagged in catalog-service (flags: ingest_gate.v2.enable, ingest_gate.v2.hard_block).
